header: Date: 2026-09-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Sophie Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Jorge Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rachel Morgan (Elmwood CRO), Derek Huang (Elmwood Head Cloud Ops), Anita Reyes (Elmwood Legal), Samir Iqbal (Elmwood Data)
summary: Discovery focused on data residency, multi-region lockdown, log retention policies and encryption key residency. Elmwood requires strict controls for financial data (GDPR + regional lock), wants options for private deployment vs dedicated, and is worried about audit log leakage and KMS residency for HSM-managed keys. Next steps include sending SOC2/HIPAA materials, pricing for dedicated pool, and scheduling a technical deep-dive.
topics: Encryption keys: KMS vs HSM / key residency
Fallbacks, SLAs, and contract language for data deletion
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Sophie here from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Rachel Morgan: Rachel Morgan, Chief Risk Officer at Elmwood. Thanks.
[00:10] Derek Huang: Derek, Head of Cloud Ops.
[00:12] Anita Reyes: Anita, Legal counsel.
[00:15] Samir Iqbal: Samir, data eng.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Marcus Lee, SE, I'll be the technical lead today.
[00:22] Sophie: Great. Agenda — understand your compliance constraints, talk through three deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private — and then map audit/logging and key controls.
[00:31] Rachel: High level, Elmwood is a trust and custodial financial services firm. We're expanding our ML workflows and need to evaluate vendors for PII handling, residency and auditability. We have EU clients, some US healthcare-adjacent data, though not direct PHI, but legal wants HIPAA to be considered as a bar.
[00:47] Sophie: Understood. Marcus, do you want to start with how Redwood addresses region lock and what options we have?
[00:51] Marcus: Yeah. So, quick summary — for hosted we have regional endpoints and can pin a model to a region, but hosted is multi-tenant control plane. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in a region with network isolation from other tenants, and Private is a VPC or on-prem control plane so ELmw — sorry, Elmwood — keeps control.
[01:12] Derek: Quick clarification — when you say "pin to a region" for hosted, is that contractual? We can't afford data to leave EU for those EU clients.
[01:20] Marcus: On hosted we provide region scoping and can enforce processing in eu-west-1 for those orgs, but control plane metadata (e.g., job status) may still touch our control plane, which can be routed through other regions unless you take Private. For strict contractual region-lock you want Private or Dedicated with region-specific SLO and contractual clause.
[01:38] Anita: Legal question — can you guarantee encryption key residency? We require keys to reside in our EU KMS and be under our control for certain datasets.
[01:46] Jorge Alvarez: Short answer: with Private deployments we integrate with customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) and can support HSM backed keys. For Dedicated we offer CMK integration via cloud KMS in the customer account (if running in their cloud) or BYOK through our partner HSM flow. Hosted generally uses Redwood-managed KMS and we rotate keys — not acceptable for your requirement, I suspect.
[02:04] Samir: So in Dedicated are the GPUs in our AWS account or Redwood's?
[02:09] Marcus: Dedicated pools are in Redwood-managed accounts but logically isolated; however we can offer a variation where the compute layer runs in a customer VPC — it's more of a Private deployment. If you need compute under your tenancy (for compliance), that's Private/on-prem.
[02:25] Rachel: Important: for EU clients we need both compute and KMS to be within EU; logs must not contain raw request text after 30 days and must be deletable on request. Does Redwood's logging pipeline allow redaction and timed deletion?
[02:37] Marcus: Yes, there's a few layers. We have request-level audit logs and token-level tracing in the console for debugging. We can configure log retention windows per-tenant for Dedicated/Private and also support automatic redaction rules to remove raw prompts or mask PII. Hosted has a default retention policy that might be longer but we can negotiate for enterprise.
[02:55] Anita: I need specifics for contract: how do you prove deletion? Is there an attestable procedure?
[03:00] Sophie: We provide deletion APIs and audit logs showing deletion events. For Private deployments the audit trail remains in your control. We can provide runbooks and a contractual SLA for deletion timelines; we'll send the standard deletion process and examples.
[03:13] [00:03:14] Speaker 2: Uh yeah, can you also share sample sanitized log output, because legal wants to see format.
[03:20] Jorge: Absolutely, we'll prepare a sample sanitized audit-log export and include fields masked.
[03:24] Derek: Another question — how do you handle cache or prefix caching? If a prompt is cached and served to another user accidentally, that's a risk.
[03:33] Marcus: Good point. Redwood's KV/prefix cache is tenant-scoped; we don't co-mingle across tenants. For Hosted there's multi-tenant processes but with logical separation. For strict isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private. We can also disable caching for certain routes that handle sensitive PII.
[03:48] Rachel: On GDPR Article 32/33/34 obligations — we need support for data subject requests and swift breach notification. What's Redwood's approach?
[03:57] Sophie: We have incident response runbooks, we support data exports for DSARs, and for Private deployments Elmwood would run the control plane and could handle DSARs internally. For Hosted we commit to notify within X hours in our SOC2 incident policy; we'll include the exact timeframe in the docs.
[04:11] Anita: SOC2 report — production date and last external audit?
[04:14] Sophie: Our SOC2 Type II report is available; last audit was Q2 2026. I'll send the bridge letter and report redacted for operational details.
[04:23] [00:04:24] Speaker 1: Sorry, quick aside — pricing. If we go Dedicated with a EU-only cluster, how much delta vs hosted?
[04:31] Marcus: Rough ballpark — Dedicated has a fixed monthly commitment plus lower per-token variable cost; Private on-prem is higher due to deployment overhead. We'll send two scenarios: small pilot dedicated pool (X GPUs) and a larger steady-state.
[04:42] Samir: For logs retention, what granularity? Like per-route, per-model?
[04:47] Jorge: We support per-route retention and per-org retention. You can set the route to retain verbose tokens for 7 days and metadata for 365 days, for example.
[04:56] Rachel: We also need immutable audit trails for compliance audits — chain-of-custody. Can Redwood produce tamper-evident logs or integrate with our SIEM?
[05:05] Marcus: We can stream logs to your SIEM via forwarders. For tamper evidence you can stream to an append-only store (e.g., S3 with Object Lock) or an external ledger. With Private you control that storage so you get immutability.
[05:18] Anita: On HIPAA — you said you haven't been a HIPAA covered entity, can you sign a BAA?
[05:24] Sophie: We do support BAAs for customers with covered workloads; we'll include the standard BAA template and any carveouts. We'll flag the parts around hosted control plane metadata again.
[05:33] Derek: About telemetry — does Redwood collect model telemetry (like token-level correctness signals) that could include user text?
[05:40] Jorge: We collect telemetry for performance and quality if enabled, but it's configurable. For enterprise clients we default to minimal telemetry and you can opt out, with the tradeoff of less product analytics.
[05:50] [00:05:51] Speaker 3: There's also the question of key rotation — if we manage keys, can we roll keys without downtime?
[05:58] Marcus: With KMS integration and HSM, rotation is seamless when using envelope encryption; we support key rotation flows and a short transition window for caches. We'll share technical docs.
[06:09] Rachel: Is there any scenario where model snapshots or intermediate embeddings leave the region? For example, embedding indices stored for search — residency requirement applies.
[06:18] Jorge: Embeddings and model artifacts follow the deployment region for Dedicated/Private. With Hosted we pin to region too but metadata may be outside; we recommend Dedicated if you store embeddings subject to residency. Also we offer an ingest-only pipeline that keeps indices in customer-managed storage.
[06:32] Samir: For our internal compliance, legal wants assurance logs don't leak prompt text in stack traces. Do you have examples of sanitized stack traces?
[06:41] Marcus: Yes, our ops team strips request payloads from traces for enterprise. For Private you'll get full control. We'll attach sample sanitized traces to the doc pack.
[06:50] Anita: Contractually we need sub-processing lists — who are your subcontractors and where are they located?
[06:56] Sophie: We'll share an up-to-date subprocessor list and country locations; we rotate sometimes so it's in the security pack.
[07:02] [00:07:03] Derek: On data deletion — if a client requests deletion for EU data, do you delete tokens from KV cache and any model fine-tuning artifacts?
[07:11] Jorge: We don't persist customer data into model training pipelines unless explicitly opted in. KV caches and persistent artifacts can be zeroed or deleted; there are documented hooks for deletion and confirmation in the audit log.
[07:22] Rachel: We have one more regulatory nuance — some of our clients are under UK financial regs which require data to be physically stored in the UK and cannot be transferred even for backups.
[07:33] Marcus: That's doable with Private deployments in a UK region and S3 with Lock; for backups we can ensure backup replicas remain in-region under Dedicated/Private.
[07:41] Anita: On encryption-at-rest, can you provide algorithm and cipher details?
[07:46] Jorge: We use AES-256-GCM for data at rest and TLS 1.3 for in-transit; HSM-backed KMS supports FIPS-certified modules where required — we'll include configs.
[07:56] [00:07:57] Speaker 2: There's a short question from Samir in chat: what about redaction rules — are they regex based or ML-based?
[08:03] Samir (chat): // redaction rules: regex vs ML?
[08:05] Marcus: We support both. You can have regex redactors + ML PII detectors for probabilistic redaction. For high assurance, combine both and route high-sensitivity inputs to dedicated non-cached endpoints.
[08:18] Rachel: For evidence to auditors, would Redwood provide a walkthrough or demo of deletion process?
[08:23] Sophie: Yes, we can run a live demo or record one for auditors. We'll schedule the technical deep-dive and do that as part of it.
[08:30] [00:08:31] Speaker 1: Pricing again — you said a pilot could be cheaper, what's typical pilot commitment?
[08:36] Marcus: Pilots vary; often a 3-month dedicated pilot with a small GPU pool and ingress/request caps is common. We'll include a sample contract in the follow-up.
[08:44] Anita: A legal note: we'll need indemnity language for cross-border processing — can your legal team handle that?
[08:50] Sophie: Yes, our legal team negotiates standard clauses; we'll provide an initial redline-ready contract and BAA.
[08:57] [00:08:58] Speaker 4: Are there any known limitations for on-prem deployment regarding model versions or kernel support?
[09:03] Jorge: On-prem supports the same model catalog but hardware constraints may limit very large models; we publish compatibility matrices. For some quantization kernels we rely on OS-level drivers; our engineers help certify customer hardware.
[09:17] Derek: For Private we may want to run in our GCP tenancy — is that supported?
[09:21] Marcus: Yes, Private can run in major clouds or on-prem. There is some engineering integration work for customer tenancy but it's supported.
[09:29] Rachel: Here's an operational question — during failover our ops team needs to know if there's a graceful fallback policy to a lower-tier model outside region. We can't allow data to be served from a non-EU region in failover.
[09:40] Marcus: You can configure routing policies to never failover outside region; Redwood supports region-aware fallback policies and model variant rules. If you choose Hosted and allow cross-region fallback it's possible, but we can lock it to EU-only.
[09:53] Samir: For auditing we want a hash of deleted content as proof it existed but is removed — some regulators accept a hash.
[09:59] Jorge: We can provide deletion receipts with SHA hashes stored in an append-only log at your side; that's a pattern we've implemented.
[10:07] Anita: We need the risk matrix — what are the top 5 residual risks if we go hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[10:13] Sophie: We'll prepare a residual risk comparison document in the follow-up — but quick summary: hosted = faster time-to-value, higher residual metadata exposure; dedicated = good isolation, Redwood-managed infra; private = most control, highest ops overhead.
[10:27] [00:10:28] Speaker 2: Any other questions from Elmwood side?
[10:31] Rachel: Not right now, just to reiterate — EU compute + EU KMS + 30-day raw prompt retention max, deletion on request, sample sanitized logs for auditors, and BAA.
[10:46] Sophie: Great — recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2/BAA/hipaa appendix, redaction playbook, sample sanitized logs, and dedicated pricing. We'll propose Nov 2 for a deep-dive.
[10:57] Derek: Sounds good.
[10:59] Anita: Thanks, we'll look for docs.
[11:02] Sophie: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links to the security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security/elmwood) and pricing spreadsheet. Bye.
[11:12] [00:11:13] End of recording.
